Welcome back to the Weekly Tokimeki Question! Today we’re keeping it simple: what is one small thing that made you smile today? ✨

For Marie, it was recently, while she was taking a walk with her son, when he got interested in a fallen leaf and picked it up, and it was so cute. His lively, happy expression made her smile.

It doesn’t have to be big. Sometimes life’s greatest joys can be found in the smallest moments, the ones we tend to rush past.

Think of that small thing and stay with the feeling for just a few seconds. Notice how it feels in your body. This is how we begin to cultivate our sensitivity to Tokimeki, by slowing down, noticing joy, and allowing ourselves to fully experience it.

📌 Share yours with us below, in a photo or a comment! We’ll be featuring some of your answers in an upcoming post💛

#artoftokimeki #reflection #journalprompt #journaling #sparkjoy

When we think about tokimeki, there are 3 main circles that you should try to keep in balance to make joy more sustainable in your life. They are：

1. Your Joy Circle: Understanding Your Joy
Finding joy for yourself is essential. It is what drives you forward. When you are fulfilled and happy, your capacity to contribute increases, and when self-care becomes possible, it becomes easier to thrive and share.

2. Your Social Circle: To Share & Amplify
Joy multiplies when shared. Understanding what sparks joy for those you care about creates stronger bonds and mutual support. When you have social joy, even personal achievements can feel more exciting.

3. Your Value Circle: What You Bring Beyond Yourself. What You Bring to the World
Through work, art, service, or innovation, contribute to the world. With external value, the practice can become much more sustainable as a lifestyle.

Your personal joy circle, your social circle, and your value circle.
All three together to create a more joyful life for you, your people, and the world.

✨Follow us as we share practices, rituals, prompts, etc. to learn how!

IQ (Intelligence Quotient) makes you smart.
EQ (Emotional Quotient) makes you kind.
TQ (Tokimeki Quotient) makes you alive.

The Tokimeki Quotient is your ability to recognize and trust what truly matters to you.

When you hone your sensitivity to what sparks joy, it becomes easier to make choices that bring more joy, meaning, and alignment into your life. And when you are living in alignment with your Tokimeki, that positive energy naturally ripples out to the people around you.

Learn how to cultivate your Tokimeki with us.

Follow @artoftokimeki for gentle reminders, inspiration, journal prompts, and reflective questions to help you keep what sparks joy at the forefront of your everyday life. 💛

In the age of AI, what will matter most about being human?

We've spent decades valuing IQ (Intelligence Quotient), and more recently, EQ (Emotional Quotient). But what if the next quotient that defines our humanity is TQ: the Tokimeki Quotient?

Takumi Kawahara, CEO of KonMari Media Inc. (and Marie Kondo's husband), shares that TQ is our ability to recognize and choose what truly sparks joy by honing our sensitivity to what matters most to us.

In a world where AI can help us think faster and do more, our uniquely human ability to sense what is meaningful becomes even more valuable. When we learn to trust our innate sense of what sparks joy, we can make decisions with greater clarity, confidence, and alignment with the life we want to live.

Here at @artoftokimeki, we'll be exploring the philosophy behind TQ and sharing practical ways to better understand and cultivate your own Tokimeki Quotient.

What do you think of this idea? We'd love to hear your thoughts below.👇
